ask.text:
YOU GATE THE PROSE OF ONE CRATE: dsse at /home/sgilda/Documents/dsse-rs.
The first standalone envelope crate in Rust. Its PROVENANCE will be read by people who know the specification better than we do, so every claim about the encoding must match the specification text.
FIND EVERY WORD THAT WOULD BE PUBLISHED. THE REGISTER FOR A CRATE PROVENANCE IS DEVELOPER DOCUMENTATION. Second person, active voice, present tense, sentence-case headings, conditions before instructions, and requirement words used precisely. No superlatives and no unverifiable performance claim; a number in a PROVENANCE carries where it was measured.

budget.basis: hand-set: policy. A release body is a NOTICE, not a comment: it says what changed, what to verify and how, so it is longer than any thread channel and shorter than a filing. The v0.10.1 notes measure 292 prose words and would have been refused under the 90-word listing-pr band. The tables, the fenced verification blocks and the corpus table are already outside the count, because `send_prose` strips fences and table rows for every channel. No corpus of release bodies is on disk, so this is a policy number.

rows.description: section-signpost-density: '#' — only 0 section cross-reference(s) = 0.00/1k words across a multi-section paper, BELOW the academic floor 0.1/1k. A long multi-section paper with essentially no
rows.reason: The finding calls this 'a multi-section paper'. It is an 805-word provenance record whose five sections are independent citations, not an argument that runs through them, so nothing in it needs to point at anything else in it. The floor of 0.1 per 1,000 words licenses 0.08 cross-references at this length.

rows.description: hyphenated-compound-density: 'secure-systems-lab' — 16 distinct hyphenated compound-modifiers (19.8/1k words, above the human ceiling) — a long tail of novel compounds reads as optimized for token density over re
rows.reason: 25 hyphenated tokens appear in the file. 4 are ISO dates (2024-05-10, 2025-11-10, 2026-07-31, 2026-08-11) and 9 are names that change identity if de-hyphenated: secure-systems-lab, agent-evidence-vectors, ed25519-dalek, dalek-cryptography, git-clones, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, CVE-2022-35929 and UTF-8. The remainder (pre-image, multi-byte, multi-signature, non-canonical, cross-check) are ordinary technical compounds, and this document's job is to name external artifacts exactly.

rows.description: absolutes-self-contradiction: 'all' — ADVISORY (absolutes lexicon): absolute claim word — every hit must be ledger-adjudicated, never batch-dismissed. Verify no hedged variant of the same claim exis
rows.reason: The one 'all' is 'Three IP addresses appear, all inside decoded bodies', which is a count I took: 0 of the three occur in the JSON text and 12 occurrences total sit inside base64 members. 0 hedge tokens appear anywhere in the file.

rows.description: absolutes-self-contradiction: 'every' — ADVISORY (absolutes lexicon): absolute claim word — every hit must be ledger-adjudicated, never batch-dismissed. Verify no hedged variant of the same claim exis
rows.reason: The one 'every' is 'it keeps every property the suite relies on', and the properties are then enumerated in the same sentence: real signatures over real PAE pre-images from an independent implementation, and one payload that is not UTF-8. That is 4 named properties rather than an open-ended claim, and 0 hedged variants appear in the file.
